intro: Searching for a dermal fillers clinic near you usually means you want somewhere convenient you can get to easily, with someone who can answer your questions before you commit. You may be thinking about lip or cheek filler for the first time, or looking to move to a clinic closer to home. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK aesthetic practitioner, who will quote you directly, with prices on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a local filler clinic usually need
need_lead: Most people want a nearby clinic they can reach without a long journey, run by someone properly trained who will talk things through first.
needs: You want a clinic close enough to get to for a consultation and any follow-up without a long trip.
You are considering dermal fillers for the first time and want to understand what is involved before booking.
You want to know who will actually carry out the treatment and what training and registration they hold.
You would like to discuss which areas you are thinking about, such as lips or cheeks, and what results are realistic.
You want to ask about aftercare and what happens if something goes wrong, before you decide.
context_heading: Understanding the rules around dermal fillers
context: Dermal fillers are classed as devices rather than medicines, and the rules are tightening. The government has set out plans for a licensing scheme for non-surgical cosmetic procedures in England, but until that is in force you need to choose a clinic carefully yourself.

Practitioners on registers such as Save Face or the JCCP, and doctors and nurses registered with the GMC or NMC, offer extra reassurance. Clinics run by regulated healthcare providers may also be registered with the CQC. A good clinic should use CE or UKCA-marked products and be able to show that its practitioners are trained in anatomy and managing complications.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say which area you are in and how far you are willing to travel for a clinic near you.
Mention whether this is your first time having dermal fillers or whether you have had them before.
Describe which areas you are thinking about, such as lips, cheeks or jawline.
Say whether you have any known allergies or medical conditions the practitioner should know about.
Mention whether you would prefer to see a doctor or nurse, or are happy with another trained practitioner.
Explain whether you want a consultation first or are ready to discuss booking treatment.
questions: Which dermal filler products do you use, and are they CE or UKCA-marked?
What training and registration do you hold for carrying out dermal fillers?
Is hyaluronidase kept on site in case of a complication?
Who will carry out my treatment, and will it be you personally?
What aftercare advice do you give, and how do I reach you if I have a concern afterwards?
What will the consultation involve, and is there a charge for it?

faqs.q: Are dermal fillers regulated in the UK?
faqs.a: Dermal fillers are treated as devices rather than medicines, and the rules are tightening. The government has set out plans for a licensing scheme for non-surgical cosmetic procedures in England, so until that is in force it is worth checking a practitioner's training and registration carefully.

faqs.q: What should I look for in a clinic near me?
faqs.a: Look for a practitioner who can show relevant training in anatomy and complication management, and who uses CE or UKCA-marked products. Registers such as Save Face or the JCCP, and registration with the GMC or NMC for doctors and nurses, offer extra reassurance.

faqs.q: Why does it matter whether hyaluronidase is on site?
faqs.a: Hyaluronidase is used to help dissolve hyaluronic acid filler if there is a problem. Asking whether it is kept on site is a sensible question when you are choosing a clinic for dermal fillers.
